content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.

content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.latin: 8:2 Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!

segments.t: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!

content.english: 8:2 For thy magnificence is elevated * above the heavens.

segments.t: Quóniam eleváta est magnificéntia tua, * super cælos.

segments.t: Quid est homo quod memor es eius? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?

content.english: 8:6 Thou hast made him a little less than the angels, thou hast crowned him with glory and honour: * and hast set him over the works of thy hands.

segments.t: In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum: * et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.

content.latin: 23:6 Hæc est generátio quæréntium eum, * quæréntium fáciem Dei Iacob.

Ante torum huius Vírginis frequentáte nobis dúlcia cántica drámatis.

content.english: ℣. In thy comeliness and thy beauty.

content.latin: ℟. Inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
content.english: ℟. Go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.

segments.t: Inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

content.latin: 1 Osculétur me ósculo oris sui, quia melióra sunt úbera tua vino,
content.english: 1 Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth: for thy breasts are better than wine,

segments.t: Osculétur me ósculo oris sui, quia melióra sunt úbera tua vino,

content.latin: 2 Fragrántia unguéntis óptimis. Oleum effúsum nomen tuum; ídeo adolescéntulæ dilexérunt te.
content.english: 2 Smelling sweet of the best ointments. thy name is as oil poured out: therefore young maidens have loved thee.

segments.t: Fragrántia unguéntis óptimis. Oleum effúsum nomen tuum; ídeo adolescéntulæ dilexérunt te.

content.latin: 3 Trahe me: post te currémus in odórem unguentórum tuórum. Introdúxit me rex in cellária sua; exsultábimus et lætábimur in te mémores úberum tuórum super vinum. Recti díligunt te.
content.english: 3 Draw me: we will run after thee to the odour of thy ointments. The king hath brought me into his storerooms: we will be glad and rejoice in thee, remembering thy breasts more than wine: the righteous love thee.

segments.t: Trahe me: post te currémus in odórem unguentórum tuórum. Introdúxit me rex in cellária sua; exsultábimus et lætábimur in te mémores úberum tuórum super vinum. Recti díligunt te.

content.latin: 4 Nigra sum, sed formósa, fíliæ Ierúsalem, sicut tabernácula Cedar, sicut pelles Salomónis.
content.english: 4 I am black but beautiful, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Cedar, as the curtains of Solomon.

segments.t: Nigra sum, sed formósa, fíliæ Ierúsalem, sicut tabernácula Cedar, sicut pelles Salomónis.

content.latin: 5 Nolíte me consideráre quod fusca sim, quia decolorávit me sol. Fílii matris meæ pugnavérunt contra me, posuérunt me custódem in víneis, víneam meam non custodívi.
content.english: 5 Do not consider me that I am brown, because the sun hath altered my colour: the sons of my mother have fought against me, they have made me the keeper in the vineyards: my vineyard I have not kept.

segments.t: Nolíte me consideráre quod fusca sim, quia decolorávit me sol. Fílii matris meæ pugnavérunt contra me, posuérunt me custódem in víneis, víneam meam non custodívi.

content.latin: 6 Indica mihi, quem díligit ánima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in merídie, ne vagári incípiam post greges sodálium tuórum.
content.english: 6 Show me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou liest in the midday, lest I begin to wander after the flocks of thy companions.

segments.t: Indica mihi, quem díligit ánima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in merídie, ne vagári incípiam post greges sodálium tuórum.

content.latin: 7 Si ignóras te, o pulchérrima inter mulíeres, egrédere et abi post vestígia gregum, et pasce hædos tuos iuxta tabernácula pastórum.
content.english: 7 If thou know not thyself, O fairest among women, go forth, and follow after the steps of the flocks, and feed thy kids beside the tents of the shepherds.

segments.t: Si ignóras te, o pulchérrima inter mulíeres, egrédere et abi post vestígia gregum, et pasce hædos tuos iuxta tabernácula pastórum.

content.latin: 8 Equitátui meo in cúrribus pharaónis assimilávi te, amíca mea.
content.english: 8 To my company of horsemen, in Pharao's chariots, have I likened thee, O my love.

segments.t: Equitátui meo in cúrribus pharaónis assimilávi te, amíca mea.

content.latin: 9 Pulchræ sunt genæ tuæ sicut túrturis, collum tuum sicut monília.
content.english: 9 Thy cheeks are beautiful as the turtledove's, thy neck as jewels.

content.latin: 14 Ecce tu pulchra es, amíca mea, ecce tu pulchra es; óculi tui columbárum.
content.english: 14 Behold thou art fair, O my love, behold thou art fair, thy eyes are as those of doves.

content.latin: 15 Ecce tu pulcher es, dilécte mi, et decórus. Léctulus noster flóridus,

segments.t: Ecce tu pulcher es, dilécte mi, et decórus. Léctulus noster flóridus,

content.english: Psalm 44 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 44

content.latin: 44:2 Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.
content.english: 44:2 My heart hath uttered a good word; * I speak my works to the King.

segments.t: Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.

content.latin: 44:2 Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.
content.english: 44:2 My tongue is the pen of a scrivener * that writeth swiftly.

segments.t: Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.

content.latin: 44:3 Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
content.english: 44:3 Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in thy lips; * therefore hath God blessed thee for ever.

segments.t: Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.

content.latin: 44:4 Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.
content.english: 44:4 Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, * O thou most mighty.

segments.t: Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.

content.latin: 44:5 Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
content.english: 44:5 With thy comeliness and thy beauty * set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.

segments.t: Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.

content.latin: 44:5 Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
content.english: 44:5 Because of truth and meekness and justice: * and thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.

segments.t: Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.

content.latin: 44:6 Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.
content.english: 44:6 Thy arrows are sharp: under thee shall people fall, * into the hearts of the king’s enemies.

segments.t: Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.

content.latin: 44:7 Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.
content.english: 44:7 Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: * the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.

segments.t: Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.

content.latin: 44:8 Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.
content.english: 44:8 Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity: * therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

segments.t: Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.

content.latin: 44:9 Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.
content.english: 44:9 Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume thy garments, from the ivory houses: * out of which the daughters of kings have delighted thee in thy glory.

segments.t: Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.

content.latin: 44:10 Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.
content.english: 44:10 The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing; * surrounded with variety.

segments.t: Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.

content.latin: 44:11 Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.
content.english: 44:11 Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear: * and forget thy people and thy father’s house.

segments.t: Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.

content.latin: 44:12 Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.
content.english: 44:12 And the king shall greatly desire thy beauty; * for he is the Lord thy God, and him they shall adore.

segments.t: Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.

content.latin: 44:13 Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.
content.english: 44:13 And the daughters of Tyre with gifts, * yea, all the rich among the people, shall entreat thy countenance.

segments.t: Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.

content.latin: 44:14 Omnis glória eius fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.
content.english: 44:14 All the glory of the king’s daughter is within, * in golden borders, clothed round about with varieties.

segments.t: Omnis glória eius fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.

content.latin: 44:15 Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.
content.english: 44:15 After her shall virgins be brought to the king: * her neighbours shall be brought to thee.

segments.t: Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.

content.latin: 44:16 Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.
content.english: 44:16 They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing: * they shall be brought into the temple of the king.

segments.t: Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.

content.latin: 44:17 Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.
content.english: 44:17 Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: * thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.

segments.t: Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.

content.latin: 44:18 Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
content.english: 44:18 They shall remember thy name * throughout all generations.

segments.t: Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.

content.latin: 44:18 Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 44:18 Therefore shall people praise thee for ever; yea, * for ever and ever.

segments.t: Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: Adest nobis, dilectíssimi, optátus dies beátæ ac venerábilis semper Vírginis Maríæ; ídeo cum summa exsultatióne gáudeat terra nostra, tantæ Vírginis illustráta natáli. Hæc est enim flos campi, de qua ortum est pretiósum lílium convállium, per cuius partum mutátur natúra protoplastórum, delétur et culpa. Præcísum est in ea illud Hevæ infelicitátis elógium, quo dícitur: In dolóre páries fílios tuos; quia ista in lætítia Dóminum péperit.
content.english: Dearly beloved brethren, the day for which we have longed, the Feast-day of the Blessed and Worshipful and Ever-Virgin Mary, that day is come. Let our land laugh and sing with merriment, bathed in the glory of this great Virgin's rising. She is the flower of the fields on which the priceless lily of the valleys hath blossomed. This is she whose delivery changed the nature that we draw from our first parents, and cleansed away their offence. At her that dolorous sentence which was pronounced over Eve ended its course to her it was never said: “In sorrow thou shalt bring forth children.” Gen. iii. 16. She brought forth a Child, even the Lord, but she brought Him forth, not in sorrow, but in joy.

content.latin: Heva enim luxit, ista exsultávit: Heva lácrimas, María gáudium in ventre portávit; quia illa peccatórem, ista édidit innocéntem. Mater géneris nostri pœnam íntulit mundo, Génetrix Dómini nostri salútem íntulit mundo. Auctrix peccáti Heva, auctrix mériti María. Heva occidéndo óbfuit, María vivificándo prófuit. Illa percússit, ista sanávit. Pro inobediéntia enim obediéntia commutátur, fides pro perfídia compensátur.
content.english: Eve wept, but Mary laughed. Eve's womb was big with tears, but Mary's womb was big with gladness. Eve gave birth to a sinner, but Mary gave birth to the sinless One. The mother of our race brought punishment into the world, but the Mother of our Lord brought salvation into the world. Eve was the foundress of sin, but Mary was the foundress of righteousness. Eve welcomed death, but Mary helped in life. Eve smote, but Mary healed. For Eve's disobedience, Mary offered obedience and for Eve's unbelief, Mary offered faith.

content.latin: Plaudat nunc órganis María, et inter velóces artículos týmpana puérperæ cóncrepent. Cóncinant lætántes chori, et alternántibus módulis dulcísona cármina misceántur. Audíte ígitur, quemádmodum tympanístria nostra cantáverit; ait enim: Magníficat ánima mea Dóminum: et exsultávit spíritus meus in Deo, salutári meo. Quia respéxit humilitátem ancíllæ suæ: ecce enim ex hoc beátam me dicent omnes generatiónes. Quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est. Causam ígitur invalescéntis erráti, miráculum novi partus evícit; et Hevæ planctum Maríæ cantus exclúsit.
content.english: Let Mary now make a loud noise upon the organ, and between its quick notes let the rattling of the Mother's timbrel be heard. Let the gladsome choirs sing with her, and their sweet hymns mingle with the changing music. Hearken to what a song her timbrel will make accompaniment. She saith: “My soul doth magnify the Lord, and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. For He hath regarded the lowliness of His hand-maiden, for, behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed for He That is Mighty hath done to me great things.” The new miracle of Mary's delivery hath effaced the curse of the frail backslider, and the singing of Mary hath silenced the wailing of Eve.

content.latin: In Isaía légimus: Generatiónem eius quis enarrábit? Non ergo putémus Evangelístam Prophétæ esse contrárium, ut quod ille impossíbile dixit effátu, hic narráre incípiat: quia ibi de generatióne Divinitátis, hic de incarnatióne est dictum. A carnálibus autem cœpit, ut per hóminem, Deum díscere incipiámus. Fílii David, fílii Abraham. Ordo præpósterus, sed necessário commutátus. Si enim primum posuísset Abraham et póstea David, rursus ei repeténdus fúerat Abraham, ut generatiónis séries texerétur.
content.english: In Isaiah liii. 8 we read: “Who shall declare His generation?” Let us not think that there is any contradiction between the Prophet and the Evangelist, because the Prophet saith that this thing cannot be done, and the Evangelist beginneth by doing it. The one speaketh of the generation of the Divine (Word by the Eternal Father,) the other of the (family in which the) Incarnation took place. Matthew beginneth with carnal things, that by learning of men we may go on to learn of God. “The Son of David, the son of Abraham.” The reversal of the order in these clauses is a needful change. If Abraham had been put first and David afterwards, Abraham would have had to be taken again, in order to marshal the pedigree properly.

content.latin: Ideo autem, céteris prætermíssis, horum fílium nuncupávit, quia ad hos tantum facta est de Christo repromíssio. Ad Abraham: In sémine, inquit, tuo benedicéntur omnes gentes, quod est Christus. Ad David: De fructu ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam. Iudas autem génuit Phares et Zaram de Thamar. Notándum, in genealogía Salvatóris nullam sanctárum assúmi mulíerum, sed eas quas Scriptúra reprehéndit; ut, qui propter peccatóres vénerat, de peccatóribus nascens, ómnium peccáta deléret. Unde et in consequéntibus Ruth Moabítis pónitur, et Bethsabée uxor Uríæ.
content.english: Matthew first calleth Christ the Son of these twain Abraham and David without making mention of the others, because unto these twain only was promise of Christ made unto Abraham, where it is said: “In thy seed” that is, in Christ “shall all the nations of the earth be blessed,” Gen. xxii. 18 and unto David, in the words “Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.” Ps. cxxxi, 11 “And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar.” It is to be remarked that in the genealogy of the Saviour none of the holy women are named, but those women only are named against whom the Scripture hath to say something amiss. He Who came to save sinners was born of sinners, that He might wash away all sin. Afterwards are named Ruth, who was a Moabitess, and Bathsheba, who had been the wife of Uriah.

content.latin: Iacob autem génuit Ioseph. Hunc locum obiécit nobis Iuliánus Augústus de dissonántia Evangelistárum, cur Evangelísta Matthǽus Ioseph díxerit fílium Iacob et Lucas eum fílium appellárit Heli; non intéllegens consuetúdinem Scripturárum, quod alter secúndum natúram, alter secúndum legem ei pater sit. Scimus enim hoc per Móysen, Deo iubénte, præcéptum, ut, si frater aut propínquus absque líberis mórtuus fúerit, álius accípiat uxórem ad suscitándum semen fratris vel propínqui sui. Ioseph virum Maríæ. Cum virum audíeris, suspício tibi non súbeat nuptiárum; sed recordáre consuetúdinis Scripturárum, quod sponsi viri, et sponsæ vocéntur uxóres.
content.english: And Jacob begat Joseph. Julian Augustus citeth this passage as an example of the lack of harmony among the Evangelists. Matthew the Evangelist saith that Joseph was the son of Jacob; Luke calleth him the son of Eli. But Julian did not understand scriptural custom. One writer may refer to a father according to nature, another to a father according to the law. We know that by God's command Moses laid down a law that should a man die without children his brother or his nearest relative was to marry the widow to raise up seed to the dead man. Joseph was the husband of Mary. When you hear the word husband do not entertain the notion of marriage in the usual sense. In the language of the Scriptures a betrothed pair were often called husband and wife.

content.latin: 148:1 Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.
content.english: 148:1 Praise ye the Lord from the heavens * praise ye him in the high places.

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.

content.latin: 148:2 Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.
content.english: 148:2 Praise ye him, all his angels: * praise ye him, all his hosts.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.

content.latin: 148:3 Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.
content.english: 148:3 Praise ye him, O sun and moon: * praise him, all ye stars and light.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.

content.latin: 148:4 Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.
content.english: 148:4 Praise him, ye heavens of heavens: * and let all the waters that are above the heavens, praise the name of the Lord.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.

content.latin: 148:5 Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 148:5 For he spoke, and they were made: * he commanded, and they were created.

segments.t: Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.

content.latin: 148:6 Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
content.english: 148:6 He hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages: * he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away.

segments.t: Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.

content.latin: 148:7 Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.
content.english: 148:7 Praise the Lord from the earth, * ye dragons, and all ye deeps:

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.

content.latin: 148:8 Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:
content.english: 148:8 Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds * which fulfill his word:

segments.t: Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:

content.latin: 148:9 Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.
content.english: 148:9 Mountains and all hills, * fruitful trees and all cedars:

segments.t: Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.

content.latin: 148:10 Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:
content.english: 148:10 Beasts and all cattle: * serpents and feathered fowls:

segments.t: Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:

content.latin: 148:11 Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.
content.english: 148:11 Kings of the earth and all people: * princes and all judges of the earth:

segments.t: Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.

content.latin: 148:12 Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.
content.english: 148:12 Young men and maidens: let the old with the younger, praise the name of the Lord: * For his name alone is exalted.

segments.t: Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.

content.latin: 148:14 Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.
content.english: 148:14 The praise of him is above heaven and earth: * and he hath exalted the horn of his people.

segments.t: Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.

content.latin: 148:14 Hymnus ómnibus sanctis eius: * fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi.
content.english: 148:14 A hymn to all his saints: to the children of Israel, a people approaching him.

segments.t: Hymnus ómnibus sanctis eius: * fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi.

content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

segments.t: Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:

content.latin: Fámulis tuis, quǽsumus, Dómine, cæléstis grátiæ munus impertíre: ut, quibus beátæ Vírginis partus éxstitit salútis exórdium; Nativitátis eius votíva solémnitas pacis tríbuat increméntum.
content.english: Grant unto us thy servants, we beseech thee, O Lord, the gift of thy heavenly grace, unto whom Thou didst give the first sight of a Saviour as the offspring of a Blessed Virgin, and grant that this Feast, which they keep in honour of the same Virgin, may avail them unto the increase of peace.

content.latin: Nicomedíæ pássio sanctórum Mártyrum Doróthei et Gorgónii, qui, cum essent apud Diocletiánum Augústum honóres amplíssimos consecúti, et persecutiónem, quam ille Christiánis inferébat, detestaréntur, præsénte eo, iussi sunt primo appéndi, et flagris toto córpore laniári; deínde, viscéribus pelle nudátis, acéto et sale perfúndi, sicque assári in cratícula; atque, ad últimum, láqueo necári. Interiécto autem témpore, beáti Gorgónii corpus Romam delátum fuit, ac via Latína pósitum, et inde ad Basílicam sancti Petri translátum.
content.english: At Nicomedia, the holy martyrs Dorotheus and Gorgonius. They stood high at the Court of the Emperor Diocletian. They denounced in his presence the persecution which he was raising against the Christians, wherefore he caused them to be hung up, and their whole bodies torn with lashes, then to have the skin taken off their bowels, to be covered with vinegar and salt, and cooked upon a gridiron, and at the last strangled. In after times the body of the blessed Gorgonius was brought to Rome, and laid first upon the Latin Way, and afterwards in the Basilica of St Peter.

content.latin: In Sabínis, trigésimo ab Urbe milliário, sanctórum Mártyrum Hyacínthi, Alexándri et Tibúrtii.
content.english: In the land of the Sabines, at the 30th milestone from the city of Rome, the holy martyrs Hyacinth, Alexander, and Tiburtius.

content.latin: Sebáste, in Arménia, sancti Severiáni, qui, cum Licínii Imperatóris esset miles, et Quadragínta Mártyres, in cárcere deténtos frequens visitáret, hinc, iussu Lýsiæ Prǽsidis, saxo ad pedes ligáto suspénsus est, ac, verbéribus cæsus et flagris laniátus, in torméntis réddidit spíritum.
content.english: At Sebaste, under the Emperor Licinius, the holy soldier Severian. He often visited the forty martyrs while they were in prison, whereupon Lysias the President ordered him to be hung up with a stone tied to his feet, and to be beaten and torn with stripes and lashes, under the which torment he gave up the ghost.

content.latin: Eódem die pássio sancti Stratónis, qui pro Christo, ad duas árbores ligátus atque discérptus, martýrium consummávit.
content.english: On the same day, the holy martyr Straton, who, for Christ's sake, was bound to two trees and torn asunder, and so finished his testimony.

content.latin: Item sanctórum Mártyrum Rufíni et Rufiniáni fratrum.

content.english: 39:3 And he heard my prayers, * and brought me out of the pit of misery and the mire of dregs.

segments.t: Et státuit super petram pedes meos: * et diréxit gressus meos.

segments.t: Et immísit in os meum cánticum novum, * carmen Deo nostro.

segments.t: Vidébunt multi, et timébunt: * et sperábunt in Dómino.

content.latin: 39:5 Beátus vir, cuius est nomen Dómini spes eius: * et non respéxit in vanitátes et insánias falsas.
content.english: 39:5 Blessed is the man whose trust is in the name of the Lord; * and who hath not had regard to vanities, and lying follies.

segments.t: Beátus vir, cuius est nomen Dómini spes eius: * et non respéxit in vanitátes et insánias falsas.

content.latin: 39:6 Multa fecísti tu, Dómine, Deus meus, mirabília tua: * et cogitatiónibus tuis non est qui símilis sit tibi.
content.english: 39:6 Thou hast multiplied thy wonderful works, O Lord my God: * and in thy thoughts there is no one like to thee.

segments.t: Multa fecísti tu, Dómine, Deus meus, mirabília tua: * et cogitatiónibus tuis non est qui símilis sit tibi.

content.latin: 39:6 Annuntiávi et locútus sum: * multiplicáti sunt super númerum.
content.english: 39:6 I have declared and I have spoken * they are multiplied above number.

segments.t: Annuntiávi et locútus sum: * multiplicáti sunt super númerum.

content.latin: 39:7 Sacrifícium et oblatiónem noluísti: * aures autem perfecísti mihi.

segments.t: Sacrifícium et oblatiónem noluísti: * aures autem perfecísti mihi.

content.latin: 39:7 Holocáustum et pro peccáto non postulásti: * tunc dixi: Ecce, vénio.
content.english: 39:7 Burnt offering and sin offering thou didst not require: * then said I, Behold I come.

segments.t: Holocáustum et pro peccáto non postulásti: * tunc dixi: Ecce, vénio.

content.english: 39:11 I have not hid thy justice within my heart: * I have declared thy truth and thy salvation.

segments.t: Non abscóndi misericórdiam tuam et veritátem tuam * a concílio multo.

content.english: 39:12 Withhold not thou, O Lord, thy tender mercies from me: * thy mercy and thy truth have always upheld me.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, ne longe fácias miseratiónes tuas a me: * misericórdia tua et véritas tua semper suscepérunt me.

content.latin: Rector potens, verax Deus,
content.english: O God of truth, O Lord of might,

content.latin: Qui témperas rerum vices,
content.english: Who orderest time and change aright,

content.latin: Splendóre mane illúminas,
content.english: Who send’st the early morning ray,

content.latin: Et ígnibus merídiem:
content.english: And light’st the glow of perfect day:

content.latin: Exstíngue flammas lítium,
content.english: Extinguish thou each sinful fire,

content.latin: Aufer calórem nóxium,
content.english: And banish every ill desire;

content.latin: Confer salútem córporum,
content.english: And while thou keep’st the body whole,

content.latin: Verámque pacem córdium.
content.english: Shed forth thy peace upon the soul.

content.english: Doth live and reign eternally.

content.english: Psalm 40 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 40

content.latin: 40:2 Beátus qui intéllegit super egénum, et páuperem: * in die mala liberábit eum Dóminus.
content.english: 40:2 Blessed is he that understandeth concerning the needy and the poor: * the Lord will deliver him in the evil day.

segments.t: Beátus qui intéllegit super egénum, et páuperem: * in die mala liberábit eum Dóminus.

content.latin: 40:3 Dóminus consérvet eum, et vivíficet eum, et beátum fáciat eum in terra: * et non tradat eum in ánimam inimicórum eius.
content.english: 40:3 The Lord preserve him and give him life, and make him blessed upon the earth: * and deliver him not up to the will of his enemies.

segments.t: Dóminus consérvet eum, et vivíficet eum, et beátum fáciat eum in terra: * et non tradat eum in ánimam inimicórum eius.

content.latin: 40:4 Dóminus opem ferat illi super lectum dolóris eius: * univérsum stratum eius versásti in infirmitáte eius.
content.english: 40:4 The Lord help him on his bed of sorrow: * thou hast turned all his couch in his sickness.

segments.t: Dóminus opem ferat illi super lectum dolóris eius: * univérsum stratum eius versásti in infirmitáte eius.

content.latin: 40:5 Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei: * sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.
content.english: 40:5 I said: O Lord, be thou merciful to me: * heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee.

segments.t: Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei: * sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.

content.latin: 40:6 Inimíci mei dixérunt mala mihi: * Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen eius?
content.english: 40:6 My enemies have spoken evils against me: * when shall he die and his name perish?

segments.t: Inimíci mei dixérunt mala mihi: * Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen eius?

content.latin: 40:7 Et si ingrediebátur ut vidéret, vana loquebátur: * cor eius congregávit iniquitátem sibi.
content.english: 40:7 And if he came in to see me, he spoke vain things: * his heart gathered together iniquity to itself.

segments.t: Et si ingrediebátur ut vidéret, vana loquebátur: * cor eius congregávit iniquitátem sibi.

content.latin: 40:7 Egrediebátur foras, * et loquebátur in idípsum.
content.english: 40:7 He went out * and spoke to the same purpose.

segments.t: Egrediebátur foras, * et loquebátur in idípsum.

content.latin: 40:8 Advérsum me susurrábant omnes inimíci mei: * advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi.
content.english: 40:8 All my enemies whispered together against me: * they devised evils to me.

segments.t: Advérsum me susurrábant omnes inimíci mei: * advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi.

content.latin: 40:9 Verbum iníquum constituérunt advérsum me: * Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?
content.english: 40:9 They determined against me an unjust word: * shall he that sleepeth rise again no more?

segments.t: Verbum iníquum constituérunt advérsum me: * Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?

content.latin: 40:10 Étenim homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi: * qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.
content.english: 40:10 For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, * who ate my bread, hath greatly supplanted me.

segments.t: Étenim homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi: * qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.

content.latin: 40:11 Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei, et resúscita me: * et retríbuam eis.
content.english: 40:11 But thou, O Lord, have mercy on me, and raise me up again: * and I will requite them.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei, et resúscita me: * et retríbuam eis.

content.latin: 40:12 In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me: * quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.
content.english: 40:12 By this I know, that thou hast had a good will for me: * because my enemy shall not rejoice over me.

segments.t: In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me: * quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.

content.latin: 40:13 Me autem propter innocéntiam suscepísti: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum.
content.english: 40:13 But thou hast upheld me by reason of my innocence: * and hast established me in thy sight for ever.

segments.t: Me autem propter innocéntiam suscepísti: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum.

content.latin: 40:14 Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * fiat, fiat.
content.english: 40:14 Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel from eternity to eternity. * So be it. So be it.

segments.t: Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * fiat, fiat.

content.latin: 41:2 Quemádmodum desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum: * ita desíderat ánima mea ad te, Deus.
content.english: 41:2 As the hart panteth after the fountains of water; * so my soul panteth after thee, O God.

segments.t: Quemádmodum desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum: * ita desíderat ánima mea ad te, Deus.

content.latin: 41:3 Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum fortem vivum: * quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dei?
content.english: 41:3 My soul hath thirsted after the strong living God; * when shall I come and appear before the face of God?

segments.t: Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum fortem vivum: * quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dei?

content.latin: 41:4 Fuérunt mihi lácrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte: * dum dícitur mihi cotídie: Ubi est Deus tuus?
content.english: 41:4 My tears have been my bread day and night, * whilst it is said to me daily: Where is thy God?

segments.t: Fuérunt mihi lácrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte: * dum dícitur mihi cotídie: Ubi est Deus tuus?

content.latin: 41:5 Hæc recordátus sum, et effúdi in me ánimam meam: * quóniam transíbo in locum tabernáculi admirábilis, usque ad domum Dei.
content.english: 41:5 These things I remembered, and poured out my soul in me: * for I shall go over into the place of the wonderful tabernacle, even to the house of God:

segments.t: Hæc recordátus sum, et effúdi in me ánimam meam: * quóniam transíbo in locum tabernáculi admirábilis, usque ad domum Dei.

content.latin: 41:5 In voce exsultatiónis, et confessiónis: * sonus epulántis.
content.english: 41:5 With the voice of joy and praise; * the noise of one feasting.

segments.t: In voce exsultatiónis, et confessiónis: * sonus epulántis.

content.latin: 41:6 Quare tristis es, ánima mea? * et quare contúrbas me?
content.english: 41:6 Why art thou sad, O my soul? * and why dost thou trouble me?

segments.t: Quare tristis es, ánima mea? * et quare contúrbas me?

content.latin: 41:6 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
content.english: 41:6 Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

segments.t: Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.

Psalmus 41(7-12)

content.latin: 41:7 Ad meípsum ánima mea conturbáta est: * proptérea memor ero tui de terra Iordánis, et Hermóniim a monte módico.
content.english: 41:7 My soul is troubled within myself: * therefore will I remember thee from the land of Jordan and Hermoniim, from the little hill.

segments.t: Ad meípsum ánima mea conturbáta est: * proptérea memor ero tui de terra Iordánis, et Hermóniim a monte módico.

content.latin: 41:8 Abýssus abýssum ínvocat, * in voce cataractárum tuárum.
content.english: 41:8 Deep calleth on deep, * at the noise of thy flood-gates.

segments.t: Abýssus abýssum ínvocat, * in voce cataractárum tuárum.

content.latin: 41:8 Ómnia excélsa tua, et fluctus tui * super me transiérunt.
content.english: 41:8 All thy heights and thy billows * have passed over me.

segments.t: Ómnia excélsa tua, et fluctus tui * super me transiérunt.

content.latin: 41:9 In die mandávit Dóminus misericórdiam suam: * et nocte cánticum eius.
content.english: 41:9 In the daytime the Lord hath commanded his mercy; * and a canticle to him in the night.

segments.t: In die mandávit Dóminus misericórdiam suam: * et nocte cánticum eius.

content.latin: 41:9 Apud me orátio Deo vitæ meæ, * dicam Deo: Suscéptor meus es.
content.english: 41:9 With me is prayer to the God of my life. * I will say to God: Thou art my support.

segments.t: Apud me orátio Deo vitæ meæ, * dicam Deo: Suscéptor meus es.

content.latin: 41:10 Quare oblítus es mei? * et quare contristátus incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?
content.english: 41:10 Why hast thou forgotten me? * and why go I mourning, whilst my enemy afflicteth me?

segments.t: Quare oblítus es mei? * et quare contristátus incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?

content.latin: 41:11 Dum confringúntur ossa mea, * exprobravérunt mihi qui tríbulant me inimíci mei.
content.english: 41:11 Whilst my bones are broken, * my enemies who trouble me have reproached me;

segments.t: Dum confringúntur ossa mea, * exprobravérunt mihi qui tríbulant me inimíci mei.

content.latin: 41:11 Dum dicunt mihi per síngulos dies: Ubi est Deus tuus? * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?
content.english: 41:11 Whilst they say to me day by day: Where is thy God? * Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why dost thou disquiet me?

segments.t: Dum dicunt mihi per síngulos dies: Ubi est Deus tuus? * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?

content.latin: 41:12 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
content.english: 41:12 Hope thou in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

segments.t: Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.

content.english: Ant. But thou hast upheld me, O Lord, and hast established me in thy sight for ever.

segments.t: Ant.
Suscepísti me, Dómine: et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo.

content.latin: Et sic in Sion firmáta sum, et in civitáte sanctificáta simíliter requiévi, et in Ierúsalem potéstas mea. Et radicávi in pópulo honorificáto, et in parte Dei mei heréditas illíus, et in plenitúdine sanctórum deténtio mea.
content.english: And so was I established in Sion, and in the holy city likewise I rested, and my power was in Jerusalem. And I took root in an honourable people, and in the portion of my God his inheritance, and my abode is in the full assembly of saints.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

segments.t: Elégit eam Deus, et præelégit eam.

content.english: ℟. He hath made her to dwell in His tabernacle.

segments.t: In tabernáculo suo habitáre facit eam.

content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Fámulis tuis, quǽsumus, Dómine, cæléstis grátiæ munus impertíre: ut, quibus beátæ Vírginis partus éxstitit salútis exórdium; Nativitátis eius votíva solémnitas pacis tríbuat increméntum.
content.english: Grant unto us thy servants, we beseech thee, O Lord, the gift of thy heavenly grace, unto whom Thou didst give the first sight of a Saviour as the offspring of a Blessed Virgin, and grant that this Feast, which they keep in honour of the same Virgin, may avail them unto the increase of peace.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: Rerum, Deus, tenax vigor,
content.english: O strength and stay upholding all creation,

content.latin: Immótus in te pérmanens,
content.english: Who ever dost thyself unmoved abide,

content.latin: Lucis diúrnæ témpora
content.english: Yet day by day the light in due gradation

content.latin: Succéssibus detérminans:
content.english: From hour to hour through all its changes guide:

content.latin: Largíre lumen véspere,
content.english: Grant to life’s day a calm unclouded ending,

content.latin: Quo vita nusquam décidat,
content.english: An eve untouched by shadows of decay,

content.latin: Sed prǽmium mortis sacræ
content.english: The brightness of a holy death-bed blending

content.latin: Perénnis instet glória.
content.english: With dawning glories of th’ eternal day.

content.latin: Præsta, Pater piíssime,
content.english: Hear us, O Father, gracious and forgiving,

content.latin: Patríque compar Únice,
content.english: And thou, O Christ, the co-eternal Word,

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito
content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost, by all things living

content.latin: Regnans per omne sǽculum.
content.english: Now and to endless ages art adored.

content.english: Amen.

content.english: Ant. Thou hast saved us, O Lord, * and in thy name we will give praise for ever.

segments.t: Psalmus 43(2-9)

content.latin: 43:2 Deus áuribus nostris audívimus: * patres nostri annuntiavérunt nobis.
content.english: 43:2 We have heard, O God, with our ears: * our fathers have declared to us,

segments.t: Deus áuribus nostris audívimus: * patres nostri annuntiavérunt nobis.

content.latin: 43:2 Opus, quod operátus es in diébus eórum, * et in diébus antíquis.
content.english: 43:2 The work thou hast wrought in their days, * and in the days of old.

segments.t: Opus, quod operátus es in diébus eórum, * et in diébus antíquis.

content.latin: 43:3 Manus tua gentes dispérdidit, et plantásti eos: * afflixísti pópulos, et expulísti eos.
content.english: 43:3 Thy hand destroyed the Gentiles, and thou plantedst them: * thou didst afflict the people and cast them out.

segments.t: Manus tua gentes dispérdidit, et plantásti eos: * afflixísti pópulos, et expulísti eos.

content.latin: 43:4 Nec enim in gládio suo possedérunt terram, * et brácchium eórum non salvávit eos:
content.english: 43:4 For they got not the possession of the land by their own sword: * neither did their own arm save them.

segments.t: Nec enim in gládio suo possedérunt terram, * et brácchium eórum non salvávit eos:

content.latin: 43:4 Sed déxtera tua, et brácchium tuum, et illuminátio vultus tui: * quóniam complacuísti in eis.
content.english: 43:4 But thy right hand and thy arm, and the light of thy countenance: * because thou wast pleased with them.

segments.t: Sed déxtera tua, et brácchium tuum, et illuminátio vultus tui: * quóniam complacuísti in eis.

content.latin: 43:5 Tu es ipse Rex meus et Deus meus: * qui mandas salútes Iacob.
content.english: 43:5 Thou art thyself my king and my God, * who commandest the saving of Jacob.

segments.t: Tu es ipse Rex meus et Deus meus: * qui mandas salútes Iacob.

content.latin: 43:6 In te inimícos nostros ventilábimus cornu: * et in nómine tuo spernémus insurgéntes in nobis.
content.english: 43:6 Through thee we will push down our enemies with the horn: * and through thy name we will despise them that rise up against us.

segments.t: In te inimícos nostros ventilábimus cornu: * et in nómine tuo spernémus insurgéntes in nobis.

content.latin: 43:7 Non enim in arcu meo sperábo: * et gládius meus non salvábit me.
content.english: 43:7 For I will not trust in my bow: * neither shall my sword save me.

segments.t: Non enim in arcu meo sperábo: * et gládius meus non salvábit me.

content.latin: 43:8 Salvásti enim nos de affligéntibus nos: * et odiéntes nos confudísti.
content.english: 43:8 But thou hast saved us from them that afflict us: * and hast put them to shame that hate us.

segments.t: Salvásti enim nos de affligéntibus nos: * et odiéntes nos confudísti.

content.latin: 43:9 In Deo laudábimur tota die: * et in nómine tuo confitébimur in sǽculum.
content.english: 43:9 In God shall we glory all the day long: * and in thy name we will give praise for ever.

segments.t: In Deo laudábimur tota die: * et in nómine tuo confitébimur in sǽculum.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

Psalmus 43(10-20)

content.latin: 43:10 Nunc autem repulísti et confudísti nos: * et non egrediéris, Deus, in virtútibus nostris.
content.english: 43:10 But now thou hast cast us off, and put us to shame: * and thou, O God, wilt not go out with our armies.

segments.t: Nunc autem repulísti et confudísti nos: * et non egrediéris, Deus, in virtútibus nostris.

content.latin: 43:11 Avertísti nos retrórsum post inimícos nostros: * et qui odérunt nos, diripiébant sibi.
content.english: 43:11 Thou hast made us turn our back to our enemies: * and they that hated us plundered for themselves.

segments.t: Avertísti nos retrórsum post inimícos nostros: * et qui odérunt nos, diripiébant sibi.

content.latin: 43:12 Dedísti nos tamquam oves escárum: * et in géntibus dispersísti nos.
content.english: 43:12 Thou hast given us up like sheep to be eaten: * thou hast scattered us among the nations.

segments.t: Dedísti nos tamquam oves escárum: * et in géntibus dispersísti nos.

content.latin: 43:13 Vendidísti pópulum tuum sine prétio: * et non fuit multitúdo in commutatiónibus eórum.
content.english: 43:13 Thou hast sold thy people for no price: * and there was no reckoning in the exchange of them.

segments.t: Vendidísti pópulum tuum sine prétio: * et non fuit multitúdo in commutatiónibus eórum.

content.latin: 43:14 Posuísti nos oppróbrium vicínis nostris, * subsannatiónem et derísum his, qui sunt in circúitu nostro.
content.english: 43:14 Thou hast made us a reproach to our neighbours, * a scoff and derision to them that are round about us.

segments.t: Posuísti nos oppróbrium vicínis nostris, * subsannatiónem et derísum his, qui sunt in circúitu nostro.

content.latin: 43:15 Posuísti nos in similitúdinem géntibus: * commotiónem cápitis in pópulis.
content.english: 43:15 Thou hast made us a byword among the Gentiles: * a shaking of the head among the people.

segments.t: Posuísti nos in similitúdinem géntibus: * commotiónem cápitis in pópulis.

content.latin: 43:16 Tota die verecúndia mea contra me est, * et confúsio faciéi meæ coopéruit me.
content.english: 43:16 All the day long my shame is before me: * and the confusion of my face hath covered me.

segments.t: Tota die verecúndia mea contra me est, * et confúsio faciéi meæ coopéruit me.

content.latin: 43:17 A voce exprobrántis, et obloquéntis: * a fácie inimíci, et persequéntis.
content.english: 43:17 At the voice of him that reproacheth and detracteth me: * at the face of the enemy and persecutor.

segments.t: A voce exprobrántis, et obloquéntis: * a fácie inimíci, et persequéntis.

content.latin: 43:18 Hæc ómnia venérunt super nos, nec oblíti sumus te: * et iníque non égimus in testaménto tuo.
content.english: 43:18 All these things have come upon us, yet we have not forgotten thee: * and we have not done wickedly in thy covenant.

segments.t: Hæc ómnia venérunt super nos, nec oblíti sumus te: * et iníque non égimus in testaménto tuo.

content.latin: 43:19 Et non recéssit retro cor nostrum: * et declinásti sémitas nostras a via tua:
content.english: 43:19 And our heart hath not turned back: * neither hast thou turned aside our steps from thy way.

segments.t: Et non recéssit retro cor nostrum: * et declinásti sémitas nostras a via tua:

content.latin: 43:20 Quóniam humiliásti nos in loco afflictiónis, * et coopéruit nos umbra mortis.
content.english: 43:20 For thou hast humbled us in the place of affliction: * and the shadow of death hath covered us.

segments.t: Quóniam humiliásti nos in loco afflictiónis, * et coopéruit nos umbra mortis.

content.latin: 43:21 Si oblíti sumus nomen Dei nostri, * et si expándimus manus nostras ad deum aliénum:
content.english: 43:21 If we have forgotten the name of our God, * and if we have spread forth our hands to a strange god:

segments.t: Si oblíti sumus nomen Dei nostri, * et si expándimus manus nostras ad deum aliénum:

content.latin: 43:22 Nonne Deus requíret ista? * ipse enim novit abscóndita cordis.
content.english: 43:22 Shall not God search out these things: * for he knoweth the secrets of the heart.

segments.t: Nonne Deus requíret ista? * ipse enim novit abscóndita cordis.

content.latin: 43:22 Quóniam propter te mortificámur tota die: * æstimáti sumus sicut oves occisiónis.
content.english: 43:22 Because for thy sake we are killed all the day long: * we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.

segments.t: Quóniam propter te mortificámur tota die: * æstimáti sumus sicut oves occisiónis.

content.latin: 43:23 Exsúrge, quare obdórmis, Dómine? * exsúrge, et ne repéllas in finem.
content.english: 43:23 Arise, why sleepest thou, O Lord? * arise, and cast us not off to the end.

segments.t: Exsúrge, quare obdórmis, Dómine? * exsúrge, et ne repéllas in finem.

content.latin: 43:24 Quare fáciem tuam avértis, * oblivísceris inópiæ nostræ, et tribulatiónis nostræ?
content.english: 43:24 Why turnest thou thy face away? * and forgettest our want and our trouble?

segments.t: Quare fáciem tuam avértis, * oblivísceris inópiæ nostræ, et tribulatiónis nostræ?

content.latin: 43:25 Quóniam humiliáta est in púlvere ánima nostra: * conglutinátus est in terra venter noster.
content.english: 43:25 For our soul is humbled down to the dust: * our belly cleaveth to the earth.

segments.t: Quóniam humiliáta est in púlvere ánima nostra: * conglutinátus est in terra venter noster.

content.latin: 43:26 Exsúrge, Dómine, ádiuva nos: * et rédime nos propter nomen tuum.
content.english: 43:26 Arise, O Lord, help us * and redeem us for thy name’s sake.

segments.t: Exsúrge, Dómine, ádiuva nos: * et rédime nos propter nomen tuum.

content.latin: Fámulis tuis, quǽsumus, Dómine, cæléstis grátiæ munus impertíre: ut, quibus beátæ Vírginis partus éxstitit salútis exórdium; Nativitátis eius votíva solémnitas pacis tríbuat increméntum.
content.english: Grant unto us thy servants, we beseech thee, O Lord, the gift of thy heavenly grace, unto whom Thou didst give the first sight of a Saviour as the offspring of a Blessed Virgin, and grant that this Feast, which they keep in honour of the same Virgin, may avail them unto the increase of peace.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

segments.t: Psalmus 109

content.latin: 109:1 Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: * Sede a dextris meis:
content.english: 109:1 The Lord said to my Lord: * Sit thou at my right hand:

segments.t: Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: * Sede a dextris meis:

content.latin: 109:1 Donec ponam inimícos tuos, * scabéllum pedum tuórum.
content.english: 109:1 Until I make thy enemies * thy footstool.

segments.t: Donec ponam inimícos tuos, * scabéllum pedum tuórum.

content.latin: 109:2 Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.
content.english: 109:2 The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: * rule thou in the midst of thy enemies.

segments.t: Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.

content.latin: 109:3 Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
content.english: 109:3 With thee is the principality in the day of thy strength: in the brightness of the saints: * from the womb before the day star I begot thee.

segments.t: Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.

content.latin: 109:4 Iurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
content.english: 109:4 The Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent: * Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.

segments.t: Iurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.

content.latin: 109:5 Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.
content.english: 109:5 The Lord at thy right hand * hath broken kings in the day of his wrath.

segments.t: Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.

content.latin: 109:6 Iudicábit in natiónibus, implébit ruínas: * conquassábit cápita in terra multórum.
content.english: 109:6 He shall judge among nations, he shall fill ruins: * he shall crush the heads in the land of many.

segments.t: Iudicábit in natiónibus, implébit ruínas: * conquassábit cápita in terra multórum.

content.latin: 109:7 De torrénte in via bibet: * proptérea exaltábit caput.
content.english: 109:7 He shall drink of the torrent in the way: * therefore shall he lift up the head.

segments.t: De torrénte in via bibet: * proptérea exaltábit caput.

segments.t: Laudáte, púeri, Dóminum: * laudáte nomen Dómini.

content.latin: 112:2 (fit reverentia) Sit nomen Dómini benedíctum, * ex hoc nunc, et usque in sǽculum.

content.latin: 112:3 A solis ortu usque ad occásum, * laudábile nomen Dómini.
content.english: 112:3 From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same, * the name of the Lord is worthy of praise.

segments.t: A solis ortu usque ad occásum, * laudábile nomen Dómini.

content.latin: 112:4 Excélsus super omnes gentes Dóminus, * et super cælos glória eius.
content.english: 112:4 The Lord is high above all nations; * and his glory above the heavens.

segments.t: Excélsus super omnes gentes Dóminus, * et super cælos glória eius.

content.latin: 112:5 Quis sicut Dóminus, Deus noster, qui in altis hábitat, * et humília réspicit in cælo et in terra?
content.english: 112:5 Who is as the Lord our God, who dwelleth on high: * and looketh down on the low things in heaven and in earth?

segments.t: Quis sicut Dóminus, Deus noster, qui in altis hábitat, * et humília réspicit in cælo et in terra?

segments.t: Ut cóllocet eum cum princípibus, * cum princípibus pópuli sui.

content.latin: 121:1 Lætátus sum in his, quæ dicta sunt mihi: * In domum Dómini íbimus.
content.english: 121:1 I rejoiced at the things that were said to me: * We shall go into the house of the Lord.

segments.t: Lætátus sum in his, quæ dicta sunt mihi: * In domum Dómini íbimus.

content.latin: 121:2 Stantes erant pedes nostri, * in átriis tuis, Ierúsalem.
content.english: 121:2 Our feet were standing * in thy courts, O Jerusalem.

segments.t: Stantes erant pedes nostri, * in átriis tuis, Ierúsalem.

content.latin: 121:3 Ierúsalem, quæ ædificátur ut cívitas: * cuius participátio eius in idípsum.
content.english: 121:3 Jerusalem, which is built as a city, * which is compact together.

segments.t: Ierúsalem, quæ ædificátur ut cívitas: * cuius participátio eius in idípsum.

content.latin: 121:4 Illuc enim ascendérunt tribus, tribus Dómini: * testimónium Israël ad confiténdum nómini Dómini.
content.english: 121:4 For thither did the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord: * the testimony of Israel, to praise the name of the Lord.

segments.t: Illuc enim ascendérunt tribus, tribus Dómini: * testimónium Israël ad confiténdum nómini Dómini.

content.latin: 121:5 Quia illic sedérunt sedes in iudício, * sedes super domum David.
content.english: 121:5 Because their seats have sat in judgment, * seats upon the house of David.

segments.t: Quia illic sedérunt sedes in iudício, * sedes super domum David.

content.latin: 121:6 Rogáte quæ ad pacem sunt Ierúsalem: * et abundántia diligéntibus te:
content.english: 121:6 Pray ye for the things that are for the peace of Jerusalem: * and abundance for them that love thee.

segments.t: Rogáte quæ ad pacem sunt Ierúsalem: * et abundántia diligéntibus te:

content.latin: 121:7 Fiat pax in virtúte tua: * et abundántia in túrribus tuis.
content.english: 121:7 Let peace be in thy strength: * and abundance in thy towers.

segments.t: Fiat pax in virtúte tua: * et abundántia in túrribus tuis.

content.latin: 121:8 Propter fratres meos, et próximos meos, * loquébar pacem de te:
content.english: 121:8 For the sake of my brethren, and of my neighbours, * I spoke peace of thee.

segments.t: Propter fratres meos, et próximos meos, * loquébar pacem de te:

content.latin: 121:9 Propter domum Dómini, Dei nostri, * quæsívi bona tibi.
content.english: 121:9 Because of the house of the Lord our God, * I have sought good things for thee.

segments.t: Propter domum Dómini, Dei nostri, * quæsívi bona tibi.

segments.t: Psalmus 126

content.latin: 126:1 Nisi Dóminus ædificáverit domum, * in vanum laboravérunt qui ædíficant eam.
content.english: 126:1 Unless the Lord build the house, * they labour in vain that build it.

segments.t: Nisi Dóminus ædificáverit domum, * in vanum laboravérunt qui ædíficant eam.

content.latin: 126:1 Nisi Dóminus custodíerit civitátem, * frustra vígilat qui custódit eam.
content.english: 126:1 Unless the Lord keep the city, * he watcheth in vain that keepeth it.

segments.t: Nisi Dóminus custodíerit civitátem, * frustra vígilat qui custódit eam.

content.latin: 126:2 Vanum est vobis ante lucem súrgere: * súrgite postquam sedéritis, qui manducátis panem dolóris.
content.english: 126:2 It is vain for you to rise before light, * rise ye after you have sitten, you that eat the bread of sorrow.

segments.t: Vanum est vobis ante lucem súrgere: * súrgite postquam sedéritis, qui manducátis panem dolóris.

content.latin: 126:2 Cum déderit diléctis suis somnum: * ecce heréditas Dómini fílii: merces, fructus ventris.
content.english: 126:2 When he shall give sleep to his beloved, * behold the inheritance of the Lord are children: the reward, the fruit of the womb.

segments.t: Cum déderit diléctis suis somnum: * ecce heréditas Dómini fílii: merces, fructus ventris.

content.latin: 126:4 Sicut sagíttæ in manu poténtis: * ita fílii excussórum.
content.english: 126:4 As arrows in the hand of the mighty, * so the children of them that have been shaken.

segments.t: Sicut sagíttæ in manu poténtis: * ita fílii excussórum.

content.latin: 126:5 Beátus vir, qui implévit desidérium suum ex ipsis: * non confundétur cum loquétur inimícis suis in porta.
content.english: 126:5 Blessed is the man that hath filled the desire with them; * he shall not be confounded when he shall speak to his enemies in the gate.

segments.t: Beátus vir, qui implévit desidérium suum ex ipsis: * non confundétur cum loquétur inimícis suis in porta.

content.english: 147:1 Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem: * praise thy God, O Sion.

segments.t: Lauda, Ierúsalem, Dóminum: * lauda Deum tuum, Sion.

content.latin: 147:2 Quóniam confortávit seras portárum tuárum: * benedíxit fíliis tuis in te.
content.english: 147:2 Because he hath strengthened the bolts of thy gates * he hath blessed thy children within thee.

segments.t: Quóniam confortávit seras portárum tuárum: * benedíxit fíliis tuis in te.

content.latin: 147:3 Qui pósuit fines tuos pacem: * et ádipe fruménti sátiat te.
content.english: 147:3 Who hath placed peace in thy borders: * and filleth thee with the fat of corn.

segments.t: Qui pósuit fines tuos pacem: * et ádipe fruménti sátiat te.

content.latin: 147:4 Qui emíttit elóquium suum terræ: * velóciter currit sermo eius.
content.english: 147:4 Who sendeth forth his speech to the earth: * his word runneth swiftly.

segments.t: Qui emíttit elóquium suum terræ: * velóciter currit sermo eius.

content.latin: 147:5 Qui dat nivem sicut lanam: * nébulam sicut cínerem spargit.
content.english: 147:5 Who giveth snow like wool: * scattereth mists like ashes.

segments.t: Qui dat nivem sicut lanam: * nébulam sicut cínerem spargit.

content.latin: 147:6 Mittit crystállum suam sicut buccéllas: * ante fáciem frígoris eius quis sustinébit?
content.english: 147:6 He sendeth his crystal like morsels: * who shall stand before the face of his cold?

segments.t: Mittit crystállum suam sicut buccéllas: * ante fáciem frígoris eius quis sustinébit?

content.latin: 147:7 Emíttet verbum suum, et liquefáciet ea: * flabit spíritus eius, et fluent aquæ.
content.english: 147:7 He shall send out his word, and shall melt them: * his wind shall blow, and the waters shall run.

segments.t: Emíttet verbum suum, et liquefáciet ea: * flabit spíritus eius, et fluent aquæ.

content.latin: 147:8 Qui annúntiat verbum suum Iacob: * iustítias, et iudícia sua Israël.
content.english: 147:8 Who declareth his word to Jacob: * his justices and his judgments to Israel.

segments.t: Qui annúntiat verbum suum Iacob: * iustítias, et iudícia sua Israël.

content.latin: 147:9 Non fecit táliter omni natióni: * et iudícia sua non manifestávit eis.
content.english: 147:9 He hath not done in like manner to every nation: * and his judgments he hath not made manifest to them.

segments.t: Non fecit táliter omni natióni: * et iudícia sua non manifestávit eis.

segments.t: Et exsultávit spíritus meus: * in Deo, salutári meo.

segments.t: Quia respéxit humilitátem ancíllæ suæ: * ecce enim ex hoc beátam me dicent omnes generatiónes.

content.latin: 1:49 Quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est: * et sanctum nomen eius.
content.english: 1:49 Because he that is mighty, hath done great things to me; * and holy is his name.

segments.t: Quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est: * et sanctum nomen eius.

content.latin: 1:50 Et misericórdia eius, a progénie in progénies: * timéntibus eum.
content.english: 1:50 And his mercy is from generation unto generations, * to them that fear him.

segments.t: Et misericórdia eius, a progénie in progénies: * timéntibus eum.

content.latin: 1:51 Fecit poténtiam in brácchio suo: * dispérsit supérbos mente cordis sui.
content.english: 1:51 He hath shewed might in his arm: * he hath scattered the proud in the conceit of their heart.

segments.t: Fecit poténtiam in brácchio suo: * dispérsit supérbos mente cordis sui.

content.latin: 1:52 Depósuit poténtes de sede: * et exaltávit húmiles.

segments.t: Depósuit poténtes de sede: * et exaltávit húmiles.

content.latin: 1:53 Esuriéntes implévit bonis: * et dívites dimísit inánes.

segments.t: Esuriéntes implévit bonis: * et dívites dimísit inánes.

segments.t: Suscépit Israël púerum suum: * recordátus misericórdiæ suæ.

content.latin: Fratres: Sóbrii estóte, et vigiláte: quia adversárius vester diábolus tamquam leo rúgiens círcuit, quærens quem dévoret: cui resístite fortes in fide.
content.english: Brothers: Be sober and watch: because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom he may devour. Whom resist ye, strong in faith.

content.latin: ℟. Qui fecit cælum et terram.

content.latin: Examen conscientiæ vel Pater Noster totum secreto.
content.english: There follows an examination of conscience, or the Our Father said silently.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris: et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem: sed líbera nos a malo. Amen.
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation: But deliver us from evil. Amen.

content.latin: Confíteor Deo omnipoténti, beátæ Maríæ semper Vírgini, beáto Michaéli Archángelo, beáto Ioánni Baptístæ, sanctis Apóstolis Petro et Paulo, et ómnibus Sanctis, quia peccávi nimis, cogitatióne, verbo et ópere: percutit sibi pectus mea culpa, mea culpa, mea máxima culpa. Ídeo precor beátam Maríam semper Vírginem, beátum Michaélem Archángelum, beátum Ioánnem Baptístam, sanctos Apóstolos Petrum et Paulum, et omnes Sanctos, oráre pro me ad Dóminum Deum nostrum.
content.english: I confess to almighty God, to blessed Mary ever Virgin, to blessed Michael the Archangel, to blessed John the Baptist, to the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and to all the Saints, that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word and deed: strikes his breast through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault. Therefore I beseech blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and all the Saints, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

segments.t: Confíteor Deo omnipoténti, beátæ Maríæ semper Vírgini, beáto Michaéli Archángelo, beáto Ioánni Baptístæ, sanctis Apóstolis Petro et Paulo, et ómnibus Sanctis, quia peccávi nimis, cogitatióne, verbo et ópere:

content.latin: Misereátur nostri omnípotens Deus, et dimíssis peccátis nostris, perdúcat nos ad vitam ætérnam. Amen.

content.latin: Indulgéntiam, ✠ absolutiónem et remissiónem peccatórum nostrórum tríbuat nobis omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus. Amen.

content.latin: 4:2 Cum invocárem exaudívit me Deus iustítiæ meæ: * in tribulatióne dilatásti mihi.
content.english: 4:2 When I called upon him, the God of my justice heard me: * when I was in distress, thou hast enlarged me.

content.english: 4:3 O ye sons of men, how long will you be dull of heart? * Why do you love vanity, and seek after lying?

content.english: 4:4 Know ye also that the Lord hath made his holy one wonderful: * the Lord will hear me when I shall cry unto him.

content.latin: 4:5 Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: * quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, in cubílibus vestris compungímini.
content.english: 4:5 Be ye angry, and sin not: * the things you say in your hearts, be sorry for them upon your beds.

segments.t: Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: * quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, in cubílibus vestris compungímini.

content.latin: 4:6 Sacrificáte sacrifícium iustítiæ, et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?
content.english: 4:6 Offer up the sacrifice of justice, and trust in the Lord: * many say, Who sheweth us good things?

segments.t: Sacrificáte sacrifícium iustítiæ, et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?

content.latin: 4:7 Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.
content.english: 4:7 The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us: * thou hast given gladness in my heart.

segments.t: Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.

content.latin: 4:8 A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.
content.english: 4:8 By the fruit of their corn, their wine, and oil, * they are multiplied.

segments.t: A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.

content.latin: 4:9 In pace in idípsum * dórmiam, et requiéscam;

content.english: 4:10 For thou, O Lord, singularly * hast settled me in hope.

content.latin: 90:1 Qui hábitat in adiutório Altíssimi, * in protectióne Dei cæli commorábitur.
content.english: 90:1 He that dwelleth in the aid of the most High, * shall abide under the protection of the God of Jacob.

segments.t: Qui hábitat in adiutório Altíssimi, * in protectióne Dei cæli commorábitur.

content.latin: 90:2 Dicet Dómino: Suscéptor meus es tu, et refúgium meum: * Deus meus sperábo in eum.
content.english: 90:2 He shall say to the Lord: Thou art my protector, and my refuge: * my God, in him will I trust.

segments.t: Dicet Dómino: Suscéptor meus es tu, et refúgium meum: * Deus meus sperábo in eum.

content.latin: 90:3 Quóniam ipse liberávit me de láqueo venántium, * et a verbo áspero.
content.english: 90:3 For he hath delivered me from the snare of the hunters: * and from the sharp word.

segments.t: Quóniam ipse liberávit me de láqueo venántium, * et a verbo áspero.

content.latin: 90:4 Scápulis suis obumbrábit tibi: * et sub pennis eius sperábis.
content.english: 90:4 He will overshadow thee with his shoulders: * and under his wings thou shalt trust.

segments.t: Scápulis suis obumbrábit tibi: * et sub pennis eius sperábis.

content.latin: 90:5 Scuto circúmdabit te véritas eius: * non timébis a timóre noctúrno,
content.english: 90:5 His truth shall compass thee with a shield: * thou shalt not be afraid of the terror of the night.

segments.t: Scuto circúmdabit te véritas eius: * non timébis a timóre noctúrno,

content.latin: 90:6 A sagítta volánte in die, a negótio perambulánte in ténebris: * ab incúrsu, et dæmónio meridiáno.
content.english: 90:6 Of the arrow that flieth in the day, of the business that walketh about in the dark: * of invasion, or of the noonday devil.

segments.t: A sagítta volánte in die, a negótio perambulánte in ténebris: * ab incúrsu, et dæmónio meridiáno.

content.latin: 90:7 Cadent a látere tuo mille, et decem míllia a dextris tuis: * ad te autem non appropinquábit.
content.english: 90:7 A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand: * but it shall not come nigh thee.

segments.t: Cadent a látere tuo mille, et decem míllia a dextris tuis: * ad te autem non appropinquábit.

content.latin: 90:8 Verúmtamen óculis tuis considerábis: * et retributiónem peccatórum vidébis.
content.english: 90:8 But thou shalt consider with thy eyes: * and shalt see the reward of the wicked.

segments.t: Verúmtamen óculis tuis considerábis: * et retributiónem peccatórum vidébis.

content.latin: 90:9 Quóniam tu es, Dómine, spes mea: * Altíssimum posuísti refúgium tuum.
content.english: 90:9 Because thou, O Lord, art my hope: * thou hast made the most High thy refuge.

segments.t: Quóniam tu es, Dómine, spes mea: * Altíssimum posuísti refúgium tuum.

content.latin: 90:10 Non accédet ad te malum: * et flagéllum non appropinquábit tabernáculo tuo.
content.english: 90:10 There shall no evil come to thee: * nor shall the scourge come near thy dwelling.

segments.t: Non accédet ad te malum: * et flagéllum non appropinquábit tabernáculo tuo.

content.latin: 90:11 Quóniam Ángelis suis mandávit de te: * ut custódiant te in ómnibus viis tuis.
content.english: 90:11 For he hath given his angels charge over thee; * to keep thee in all thy ways.

segments.t: Quóniam Ángelis suis mandávit de te: * ut custódiant te in ómnibus viis tuis.

content.latin: 90:12 In mánibus portábunt te: * ne forte offéndas ad lápidem pedem tuum.
content.english: 90:12 In their hands they shall bear thee up: * lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.

segments.t: In mánibus portábunt te: * ne forte offéndas ad lápidem pedem tuum.

content.latin: 90:13 Super áspidem, et basilíscum ambulábis: * et conculcábis leónem et dracónem.
content.english: 90:13 Thou shalt walk upon the asp and the basilisk: * and thou shalt trample under foot the lion and the dragon.

segments.t: Super áspidem, et basilíscum ambulábis: * et conculcábis leónem et dracónem.

content.latin: 90:14 Quóniam in me sperávit, liberábo eum: * prótegam eum, quóniam cognóvit nomen meum.
content.english: 90:14 Because he hoped in me I will deliver him: * I will protect him because he hath known my name.

segments.t: Quóniam in me sperávit, liberábo eum: * prótegam eum, quóniam cognóvit nomen meum.

content.latin: 90:15 Clamábit ad me, et ego exáudiam eum: * cum ipso sum in tribulatióne: erípiam eum et glorificábo eum.
content.english: 90:15 He shall cry to me, and I will hear him: * I am with him in tribulation, I will deliver him, and I will glorify him.

segments.t: Clamábit ad me, et ego exáudiam eum: * cum ipso sum in tribulatióne: erípiam eum et glorificábo eum.

content.latin: 90:16 Longitúdine diérum replébo eum: * et osténdam illi salutáre meum.

segments.t: Longitúdine diérum replébo eum: * et osténdam illi salutáre meum.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Vísita, quǽsumus, Dómine, habitatiónem istam, et omnes insídias inimíci ab ea longe repélle: Ángeli tui sancti hábitent in ea, qui nos in pace custódiant; et benedíctio tua sit super nos semper.
content.english: Visit, we beseech thee, O Lord, this dwelling, and drive far from it the snares of the enemy; let thy holy angels dwell herein to preserve us in peace, and let thy blessing be always upon us.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: ℣. Benedicámus Dómino.
content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedicámus Dómino.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedícat et custódiat nos omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus, ✠ Pater, et Fílius, et Spíritus Sanctus.
content.english: Benediction. The almighty and merciful Lord, ✠ the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, bless us and keep us.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Benedícat et custódiat nos omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus, ✠ Pater, et Fílius, et Spíritus Sanctus.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: Salve, Regína, mater misericórdiæ;
content.english: Hail holy Queen, Mother of Mercy,

content.latin: vita, dulcédo et spes nóstra, salve.
content.english: our life, our sweetness, and our hope.

content.latin: Ad te clamámus éxsules fílii Hevæ.
content.english: To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve.

content.latin: Ad te suspirámus geméntes et flentes
content.english: To thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping

content.latin: In hac lacrimárum valle.
content.english: In this valley of tears.

content.latin: Eia ergo, advocáta nostra,
content.english: Turn then, most gracious Advocate,

content.latin: illos tuos misericórdes óculos ad nos convérte.
content.english: thine eyes of mercy toward us.

content.latin: Et Iesum, benedíctum fructum ventris tui,
content.english: And after this our exile show unto us

content.latin: nobis post hoc exsílium osténde.
content.english: the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus.

content.latin: O clemens, o pia, o dulcis Virgo María.
content.english: O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

content.latin: ℣. Ora pro nobis, sancta Dei Génetrix.
content.english: ℣. Pray for us, O Holy Mother of God.

segments.t: Ora pro nobis, sancta Dei Génetrix.

content.latin: ℟. Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.
content.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

segments.t: Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui gloriósæ Vírginis Matris Maríæ corpus et ánimam, ut dignum Fílii tui habitáculum éffici mererétur, Spíritu Sancto cooperánte, præparásti: da, ut, cuius commemoratióne lætámur, eius pia intercessióne, ab instántibus malis et a morte perpétua liberémur. Per eúndem Christum Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
content.english: O almighty, everlasting God, who by the cooperation of the Holy Spirit, didst prepare the body and soul of Mary, glorious Virgin and Mother, to become a worthy dwelling for Thy Son; grant that we who rejoice in her commemoration may, by her gracious intercession, be delivered from present evils and from everlasting death. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Divínum auxílium ✠ máneat semper nobíscum.
content.english: ℣. May the divine assistance ✠ remain with us always.

segments.t: Divínum auxílium ✠ máneat semper nobíscum.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.
